characters: Look for the spurious vein (vena spuria) in the wing.
Check whether vein R4+5 is strongly dipped/looped and inspect the wing-cell pattern.
For Eristalini-like candidates, inspect hind femur/tibia shape and facial profile.
For species-level work, photograph face, antenna/arista, hind leg and wing separately.
Syrphidae.notes: Image similarity is useful for narrowing candidates, but many Syrphidae species require targeted morphology.

characters: Inspect meron for hairs/setulae and the katepisternal bristle pattern.
Check vein M1 course and calypter development.
Photograph thoracic chaetotaxy dorsally and laterally.
Muscidae.notes: Species-level identification often depends on chaetotaxy and sex-specific characters.

characters: Check postscutellum development and meral setae.
Inspect facial ridge setae, arista, and thoracic bristle rows.
For difficult genera, add lateral head and abdominal dorsal views.
Tachinidae.notes: Tachinidae are often visually convergent; morphology should overrule image similarity.

characters: Inspect wing venation, especially M and R branches.
Check antennal insertion, arista position and leg modifications.
Male secondary sexual characters can be decisive; record sex where possible.
Dolichopodidae.notes: Genus/species inference from habitus alone can be unreliable.
